correctness.rationale: The Grötzsch Mycielski graph is reconstructed with exactly 11 vertices and 20 edges. Independent exhaustive BFS/union-find comparison over all 2048 subsets verifies induced-component maximum, total stage face counts (103,313,493,763,1135,1521,1821,1981,2036,2047,2048). Verified 90 codimension-one free-face pairs collapse I3 exactly to I2 and 105 pairs collapse I2 exactly to I1. Independently reconstructed sequential-element Morse matchings on all face-poset incidences at r=1,4,..,10, acyclic under directed Hasse topological ordering: only 1 critical 2-face at r=1 and (59,151,175,115,45,10,1) critical faces at dimensions 3..9 for r4..10, respectively, with empty-face matching producing one 0-cell. Discrete Morse CW models hence wedges of spheres integrally; r>=11 full simplex. Homology degree mismatch forces only the S² generator to persist through stages 1–3, later bars supported at a single stage. This complete 2048-subset computation is a proof for the finite graph, not an extrapolation.

Deshpande–Singh framework and existing computations for paths, cycles, complete multipartite, whiskered and perfect trees do not classify the higher induced-component filtration of this triangle-free nonchordal graph. Exact integral wedge classifications for every threshold, plus the unexpected I1→I2→I3 simple-homotopy plateau and complete persistent homology, give a reusable finite benchmark well beyond the already known I1 sphere.
